scenario.title: Pampa de La Joya · test against Jezero
scenario.focus: Hyperaridity, salts and fine-dust abrasion for sampling and drilling.

source.label: Open-Meteo Forecast API snapshot («current», model) taken on 2026-11-15T02:10:10Z; not live

target.name: Jezero Crater · Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler)

environment.atmosphere: CO₂ ~95 %, surface pressure ~6–7 hPa (≈0.6 % of Earth's)

grid.dataset: MRO HiRISE DTM DTEEC_045994_1985_046060_1985_U01 (Univ. of Arizona / USGS, 1 m/px)

surfaceTemperature.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, surface temperature at 18.4447°N 77.4508°E; curve = Ls 0° (northern spring equinox) by Martian local solar hour; min/max/mean over Ls 0/90/180/270 × 24 h. http://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/cgi-bin/mcdcgi.py

provenance.label: MRO HiRISE DTM DTEEC_045994_1985_046060_1985_U01 (Univ. of Arizona / USGS, 1 m/px)

notes: Centered on the Octavia E. Butler landing site (18.4447°N, 77.4508°E); the delta front is ~2 km to the west, at the edge of the window.
HiRISE DTM at 1 m averaged to 18.75 m cells before the 37.5 m grid: metric roughness (rocks, megaripples) disappears from the geometric index.
Elevation relative to the Mars reference areoid/sphere of the PDS product (negative values of ~-2.5 km are normal at Jezero).
Thermal: Mars Climate Database (model, multi-km cell), not a MEDA/Perseverance measurement; integrating MEDA series from the PDS Atmospheres Node remains a proposal.
Roughness: no equivalent radar data; metrics.roughness = null.

caveats: Geometric, not planetary, similarity index: relief geometry does not reproduce gravity, regolith, illumination or chemistry.
Missing Earth analog metrics (Pampa de La Joya).

matrix.label: Regional scale
matrix.breakdown: The grid does not resolve wheel/soil contacts, rocks or cavities; native resolution and interpolation limit the test.
matrix.action: Measure at instrument scale before designing the test.

data.dataset: MRO HiRISE DTM DTEEC_045994_1985_046060_1985_U01 (Univ. of Arizona / USGS, 1 m/px)

matrix.label: Relief · Strength vs. Breakdown
matrix.breakdown: The index does not measure physical similarity; radar roughness in dB and CPR are not interchangeable.
matrix.action: Use components and warnings to choose tasks, with no universal validity threshold.

caveats: Geometric, not planetary, similarity index: relief geometry does not reproduce gravity, regolith, illumination or chemistry.
Missing Earth analog metrics (Pampa de La Joya).

matrix.label: Gravity and static load
matrix.strength: Static load can be adjusted with vertical support for an explicit mass.
matrix.breakdown: Reduced gravity cannot be reproduced in the field on Earth; offloading weight keeps the mass and its inertia.
matrix.action: Compute F=m·g and offload; validate dynamics and terramechanics separately.

matrix.label: Atmosphere and vacuum
matrix.strength: The terrain allows testing geometry and procedures outdoors.
matrix.breakdown: Earth’s atmosphere does not reproduce the thin CO₂ gas of Mars. The pressure reference is not a site measurement.
matrix.action: Test in a chamber with controlled composition/pressure; no scalar turns Earth air into the target.

matrix.label: Quantitative local pressure
matrix.strength: No local absolute pressure on Earth: difference and ratio unknown.
matrix.breakdown: Sea-level pressure is not converted to local pressure, and there is no division by the lunar zero.
matrix.action: Keep local absolute pressure and its date; without data no difference is computed. It does not imply aerodynamic equivalence.

matrix.label: Air / surface temperature
matrix.strength: The target thermal product and the provenance of Earth weather are kept.
matrix.breakdown: Earth air temperature is not surface temperature; there is no comparable Earth surface pair or synchronized series.
matrix.action: Measure surface, air and radiative sink separately; keep nulls (including the Shackleton minimum).

data.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, surface temperature at 18.4447°N 77.4508°E; curve = Ls 0° (northern spring equinox) by Martian local solar hour; min/max/mean over Ls 0/90/180/270 × 24 h. http://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/cgi-bin/mcdcgi.py

matrix.label: Convection and thermal radiation
matrix.strength: Q_conv and Q_rad can be explored with explicit test parameters.
matrix.breakdown: Ideal vacuum: no external convection. Mars: unknown h coefficient. There is no universal thermal factor.
matrix.action: Thermal chamber and model with their own geometry/materials, conduction and heat sources.

matrix.label: Ionizing radiation
matrix.strength: Operations and shielding geometry can be tested.
matrix.breakdown: Earth’s atmosphere and magnetic field alter the environment; solar irradiance in W/m² is not ionizing dose. There is no local dosimetry.
matrix.action: Characterize spectrum, dose and shielding with dedicated tests; no scalar correction or invented dose.

matrix.label: Regolith, dust and subsurface
matrix.strength: The scenario provides regional context for mobility or drilling.
matrix.breakdown: There is no grain-size distribution, cohesion, contact moisture or mechanical strength from samples; a DEM cannot determine them.
matrix.action: Obtain samples and mechanical tests; do not infer ice or shielding from relief or CPR.

assumptions: Level ground, same mass, quasi-static vertical support; positive F_offload points upward and a negative value requires additional load.
Positive Q = heat loss. Isothermal grey surface in a large black enclosure, view factor 1; explicit h for the gas/test, not derived from pressure.
Not a full thermal balance: excludes conduction, Sun, albedo, internal dissipation and transients. External ideal vacuum: Q_conv = 0; Mars requires its own h.
limitations: Mass (kg) does not change with the body; weight is a force (N).
Vertical offloading matches only the static load on level ground; it does not reproduce inertia, dynamics, cohesion, soil confinement, traction or terramechanics.
For a wheel, the mass is the one supported by that wheel; no uniform distribution is assumed. For a drill, cutting force, torque and active thrust are not calculated.
Vacuum, convection, ionizing radiation, chemistry and dust are not offset by a universal factor. Dedicated tests are required.
Air temperature, surface temperature and radiative sink are distinct quantities. None is automatically substituted for another.
Froude number, speed, time, dose and GO/NO-GO authorization are not evaluated; no site or instrument is certified.

configuration.assumption: 350 kg teaching prototype; real Perseverance/Scarecrow mass is not inferred from their meshes. No per-wheel load split or drill mass.

policy.retention: Memory: 6 sessions; 2160 rover samples (6 h at 10 s), 256 weather observations, 500 events per session. Reloading clears everything; resetting/changing mission closes the session.

baseProfile.title: Jezero · salt sampling
baseProfile.purpose: Plan surface extraction and separate handling of saline simulants, with grain inspection and controlled abrasion.
assumptions: Static-version design proposal; not an observation, telemetry, NASA flight datasheet or validated safety threshold. All equipment is disconnected.
The rover’s only total mass is ROVER_CONFIG.massKg = 350 kg; component masses and powers are per unit and included, not added again to the rover.
massScope distinguishes rover-total, included-in-rover, external-kit and test-equipment; the remaining mass is reserved for structure, power and cabling without a validated breakdown.
Six wheels on level ground with a uniform nominal split of 350/6 kg per wheel; it does not represent load transfer on slopes or a measured distribution.
Rover power is a simultaneous nominal budget with margin; bench and external kit have separate supply. No endurance is estimated and this consumption is not attributed to Perseverance.
Sampler thrust and torque are independent actuator setpoints, not forces derived from mass times gravity, and not completed material tests.
Heated Earth bench with controlled air: linear convection h=8 and grey radiation to the enclosure; it does not represent the Martian atmosphere.
thermal describes only equipment surface and bench wall; not meteorological air, NASA/Diviner surface or real mission temperature. Area, emissivity and h are test hypotheses.
Baseline model: Qconv=h·A·(Ts−Twall); Qrad=ε·σ·A·(Ts⁴−Twall⁴), unit view factor, steady state. Excludes Sun, conduction, dust, residual gas and internal heat; not validated thermal sizing.
Operating ranges are selection targets for protected equipment, separate from wall and sample setpoints; they do not certify survival in planetary environments.
The dosimeter only defines a proposed instrument range; ambient dose rate is not applicable for lack of measurement and source. No dose is inferred from NASA images or colors.

areaM2.rationale: Effective area of the proposed capsule for the bench model.

surfaceK.rationale: Protected equipment surface setpoint; not ground or air temperature.

surroundingsK.rationale: Bench radiative wall setpoint; not an observed planetary temperature.

hWm2K.rationale: Heated Earth bench with controlled air: linear convection h=8 and grey radiation to the enclosure; it does not represent the Martian atmosphere.

emissivity.rationale: Grey emissivity assumed for design; not derived from NASA colors or textures.
